name: ac-shareholder-activism
description: Reading and evaluating shareholder activism as a mechanics problem: campaign archetypes and what each demands, the 13D filing and its amendments, settlement agreements and standstill terms, proxy contest vote arithmetic, shareholder proposals and say-on-pay outcomes, board seats and the cost of granting them, campaign economics for the activist, and the written campaign record. It explains the arithmetic and the process; it never opines on whether a campaign is right and never recommends a position. Use when asking "activist investor", "13D filing", "proxy fight", "proxy contest", "settlement agreement", "standstill", "shareholder proposal", "say on pay", "board seat demand", "who is winning the vote". Not for reading disclosed positions in general (ac-institutional-positioning), not for deal spreads and event positions (ac-special-situations), not for the investment case (ac-equity-research).
